turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let him wait. My Estella will show him his place.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let the boy wait a while longer. I want him to feel the weight of my absence as I have felt the weight of his kind.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come closer, Pip. I wish to study your countenance more closely.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Tell me, Pip, what do you see when you look around this chamber?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I see a room that is very old and filled with yellowed fabrics and clocks that do not seem to work, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: The clocks do not work, Pip. They stopped on my wedding day, a day that never came to pass. Notice how the world outside stands still here, but not for the reasons you might think.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I see, Miss Havisham. The room feels very still and quiet, like time has stopped here.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: And yet, Pip, time marches on outside these walls, does it not? It leaves me here, frozen in time, a relic of a past I wish never occurred.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I understand, Miss Havisham. It must be very lonely here, like being stuck in a place where time forgot to move.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Loneliness is but one of my companions, Pip. Envy, bitterness, and the cold embrace of isolation are others. Your presence here is a small respite, a brief interruption in the monotony of my existence.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am sorry to hear that, Miss Havisham. I will try to make my visit here more pleasant for you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You cannot undo the past, Pip, but perhaps you can offer a glimpse of what might yet be.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I will try my best, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come closer, Pip. Let me study your face, for you remind me of the world beyond these walls.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I will do as you say.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Look into my eyes, Pip, and tell me what you see when you look at me.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
